comparison.caveat: Shared-host observation, not proof of zero overhead. GBit/s is application request plus response bytes, not wire bytes. Files count one-way payload only. Separate warmup workloads do not share sessions with measured workloads. HTTP throughput uses lifecycle elapsed; request latency excludes setup, with setup-inclusive p99 also recorded for fresh connections.

file-budget-baseline.note: Outer tool session handle was unavailable after context compaction. Persisted summary directly records benchmark subprocess exit 0 and strict gate subprocess exit 1; both finished, and no matching process remains. No claim of a directly observed outer terminal exit.

verification_caveats: Fresh final bin/verify after the benchmark-driver correction exited zero without a retry or failed native suite; all 80 driver tests and existing router/live/package/browser gates pass. Preserve the earlier run with its HTTP/3 timeout separately.

Full bin/verify exited zero, but its first feature-enabled native run had 147 passes and an HTTP/3 network handshake timeout. The existing script retried and all 148 passed. Root cause is not established; do not describe this as a clean first-attempt pass.

Initial verification: default native FFI 140, feature-enabled 148 on retry, core 149, artifact 29, driver 77, router 526 with one explicit skip, and existing consumer/live MCP/zero-copy/package/browser checks pass. The corrected driver subsequently passes all 80 tests.
Initial cargo fmt invocation at a virtual workspace lacked --all and exited one; corrected cargo fmt --all passed. This was command selection, not a compile failure.
review_evidence: Fail-first tests use an extracted common helper retaining the original unchecked fetch_add-plus-insert algorithm, not an untouched pre-refactor checkout. Seven allocator assertions fail; preserving old dispatch-before-store adds an eighth failing assertion. Five positive controls pass, then all thirteen pass after the guards/order fix.

Coverage: positive IDs, zero, signed limit, repeated exhaustion, unsigned wrap, occupied entry survival, rejected Arc destruction, eight concurrent final-slot callers, clear without reuse, signed FFI error mapping, response success and two response failure paths.

Source mapping confirms all twelve store functions pair their original counter/map with the common helper and propagate Result through thirteen FFI call sites. Existing message-store allocation is unchanged. Local tests do not exhaust production global stores or prove remote reachability.

Local Gemma summary, GLM test planning and GLM review completed. Their claims were independently checked: unchecked fetch_add does wrap; aggregate per-store budgets are not 2^13; test fixture unwraps use fresh positive IDs.

Review hypothesis of a partial-dispatch leak is not supported: HttpResponseHandle.respond sends through a oneshot. Failed send drops the undispatched reader; removing the allocated writer closes its channel. No post-commit failure was found in that send.
Keep existing SeqCst ordering for controlled attribution; do not weaken ordering on unmeasured advice. Collision fails closed with the established ABI error rather than a new panic across C.

Three deterministic HTTP/1 driver tests fill the initial Hyper queue slot with the connection driver unpolled. Plain, protected and JSON helpers incorrectly return connection-was-not-ready before the fix. Waiting for poll_ready makes all three pending until the connection runs, then both requests complete on exactly one connection. All 80 driver tests pass. This is a benchmark-driver correctness fix, not a demonstrated product-stack defect.
The first two baseline processes did not log their initial retry errors. The deterministic reproduction proves missing readiness can cause a retry, not that every original reconnect had that cause.

Third old-library attempt still reconnects with corrected readiness. Isolated diagnostic captures a TLS response-body EOF on first iteration. Do not call readiness the sole reconnect cause, claim retry-free measurements, or clear HTTP/1 reliability. Full collection retains this failure condition with an overall nonzero exit rather than silently relaxing it.

The second bounded GLM review was checked against callers: JSON login and refresh already time the full operation around their helper, including readiness waits. A later connection teardown still propagates an error; no atomic liveness promise is made. Current-thread test runtimes cancel spawned tasks on test exit, including assertion failure.
methodology: Same frozen AOT driver, service and worker for both native libraries, hash-checked before every comparison process. Baseline is the previous audit checkpoint, not pre-audit master.

Fixed ABBAAB order, three processes per variant; one router worker and four native runtime threads. Every timed process and preflight wait is retained. Warmup workloads use separate sessions from measured cases.

All sixteen canonical E2EE variations plus seven native file cases, covering RawSocket/WebSocket, clear/TLS, MessagePack/CBOR, AES-GCM/XSalsa. Same ciphers, payloads and protocol work in both variants.
Preselected per-client sample budgets: native E2EE 256, Dart XSalsa 128, Dart AES 16, four clients. Files eight iterations by two clients, 64 MiB files in 4 MiB chunks.

HTTP/1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 each cover serial 2000x1, sustained streams 256x4 (256 KiB request/1 MiB response) and fresh connections 128x8. Exact byte/count, error, reconnect and finite-timing validation.

WAMP throughput uses the data window; HTTP throughput uses lifecycle elapsed. Request latency excludes setup; fresh HTTP also records setup-inclusive operation p99 and verifies the setup+request <= total invariant.
GBit/s counts application request plus response bytes, except files count only one-way payload. It is not wire bandwidth; serializer/encryption overhead is not added.

RSS is sampled after each workload. Maximum RSS is a shared-process high-water mark, not isolated workload peak allocation. HTTP driver client memory is unavailable, not zero. Small file/Dart AES samples limit tail precision.
No own tests/builds/inference overlap timed benchmarks. Unrelated host load is recorded at process boundaries, which does not prove that every sample was uncontended.

Existing production thresholds are unchanged. Passing absolute gates does not clear relative regressions, finite ID availability, earlier security performance questions or incomplete component coverage.

An unexpected HTTP connection count is a strict validation finding. All six processes are collected to retain unaffected workloads and both native variants, then the comparison exits nonzero on any finding. Retry-affected HTTP request-only latency omits failed-attempt time; lifecycle goodput includes it. Those rows cannot establish clean-request latency or no-overhead clearance.

The errors field counts terminal logical-request sample errors, not recovered attempts. Connection findings expose recovered failures even when these fields and the four transport-error counters remain zero. Byte validation checks reported request/response byte counts; no extra HTTP content-hash verification was added.

Initial 75-workload absolute run has one budget failure: buffered Dart/JSON WebSocket file lifecycle goodput 1952.258 Mbps against unchanged 2000 Mbps minimum. Other 74 workloads pass. A separate full 30-workload file confirmation is retained, regardless of outcome; no threshold or workload is weakened.

Candidate full-file confirmation also fails the same lone budget at 1900.428 Mbps. The identical full 30-workload matrix using the previous SA-007 native library fails it at 1920.826 Mbps. Each process completes 408 samples and other 29 file workloads pass. The failure is not unique to SA-008, but one baseline and two candidate absolute runs on a shared host do not establish equal performance or clear the budget. No gate threshold changed.

import hashlib
import json
import math
import statistics
import subprocess
import time
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path('.')
OUT = Path('/tmp/connectanum-sa008-resource-performance-complete')
DRIVER = Path('/tmp/connectanum-sa008-ready-http_stream')
LAUNCHER = Path('/tmp/connectanum-security-aot-launch')
SERVICE = Path('/tmp/connectanum-sa005-dart-wide-service/bundle/bin/bench_router_service')
WORKER = Path('/tmp/connectanum-sa005-dart-wide-worker/bundle/bin/wamp_client_worker')
LIBRARIES = {
    'baseline': Path('/tmp/connectanum-sa007-restart-libct_ffi.dylib'),
    'patched': Path('/tmp/connectanum-sa008-resource-libct_ffi.dylib'),
}
EXPECTED = {
    DRIVER: 'a8d92bc35e6c4fa8dfb8075d7a17b7c8dcc959fb5fb164673029f3ea991e03e1',
    SERVICE: '171ce6f5e1091556fe30a2c6a55b97af83e600155754a3398aecfb52649c5b85',
    WORKER: 'c79ed4e83c293e727a81b78bbcc2d4628311aeaeb3e1ba2d4e31b4213addd074',
    LIBRARIES['baseline']: 'd8f136020742bf910280b757aa579e7b4c67018104c2b3c5ee68156bee6a6c66',
    LIBRARIES['patched']: '2ca93e7991c50b396e37fc4e60f75fcbcbdca9f5328a1c78d7e2ae8bd176701c',
}


def digest(path):
    with path.open('rb') as stream:
        return hashlib.file_digest(stream, 'sha256').hexdigest()


def write_new(path, value):
    with path.open('x') as stream:
        json.dump(value, stream, indent=2)
        stream.write('\n')


def cpu():
    totals = dict(inference=0., virtual_machine=0., emulator=0., other=0.)
    for row in subprocess.check_output(['ps', '-axo', '%cpu,comm'], text=True).splitlines()[1:]:
        number, command = row.strip().split(maxsplit=1)
        key = ('inference' if 'llama-server' in command or 'ollama' in command else
               'virtual_machine' if 'Virtualization.framework' in command else
               'emulator' if 'qemu-system' in command else 'other')
        totals[key] += float(number)
    return {k: round(v, 1) for k, v in totals.items()}


def preflight(name):
    snapshots = []
    for _ in range(31):
        snapshot = dict(timestamp=time.time(), cpu=cpu())
        snapshots.append(snapshot)
        c = snapshot['cpu']
        if c['inference'] < 50 and c['virtual_machine'] < 600 and c['other'] < 800:
            write_new(OUT / f'{name}.preflight.json', snapshots)
            return
        time.sleep(10)
    write_new(OUT / f'{name}.preflight.json', snapshots)
    raise RuntimeError('Host remains busy; stop between benchmark processes')


def scenario_cases():
    e2ee = tomllib.loads((ROOT / 'native/bench/scenarios/wamp_e2ee_throughput.toml').read_text())['workloads']
    assert len(e2ee) == 16
    for case in e2ee:
        # Pure-Dart AES has a much slower existing CPU path than native E2EE.
        # Fix sample budgets before either variant runs; retain every sample.
        case['iterations'] = (16 if case['client_impl'] == 'dart' and case['ppt_cipher'] == 'aes256gcm'
                              else 128 if case['client_impl'] == 'dart' else 256)
    files = tomllib.loads((ROOT / 'native/bench/scenarios/wamp_file_transfer_throughput.toml').read_text())['workloads']
    selected = [
        'rawsocket_file_msgpack_64m_native',
        'rawsocket_tls_file_cbor_64m_native_segmented',
        'websocket_file_cbor_64m_native_segmented',
        'rawsocket_file_cbor_e2ee_64m_native_segmented',
        'websocket_tls_file_cbor_e2ee_64m_native_segmented',
    ]
    cases = e2ee + [next(c for c in files if c['name'] == n).copy() for n in selected]
    for case in list(cases):
        if 'file_transfer' in case['protocol'] and case.get('ppt_cipher') == 'aes256gcm':
            cases.append(dict(case, name=case['name'] + '_xsalsa', ppt_cipher='xsalsa20poly1305'))
    assert len(cases) == 23
    for protocol in ['h1', 'h2', 'h3']:
        for mode, iterations, concurrency, request, response in [
                ('serial', 2000, 1, 1024, 1024),
                ('streaming', 256, 4, 262144, 1048576),
                ('fresh', 128, 8, 1024, 1024)]:
            case = dict(name=f'{protocol}_{mode}', protocol=protocol,
                        path='/bench/stream', method='POST', iterations=iterations,
                        concurrency=concurrency, request_bytes=request,
                        response_bytes=response, request_chunk_bytes=min(request, 65536),
                        response_chunk_bytes=min(response, 131072),
                        reuse_connections=mode != 'fresh')
            if protocol != 'h1':
                case['streams_per_connection'] = 4 if mode == 'streaming' else 1
            cases.append(case)
    assert len(cases) == 32
    return cases


def warmup_iterations(case):
    if 'file_transfer' in case['protocol']:
        return 2
    return 4 if case['iterations'] == 16 else 16


def summarize(path, cases):
    summaries = []
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        row = json.loads(line)
        name = row['workload']
        case = next(c for c in cases if c['name'] == name.removeprefix('warmup_'))
        samples = row['samples']
        warmup = name.startswith('warmup_')
        iterations = warmup_iterations(case) if warmup else case['iterations']
        assert row['iterations'] == iterations and row['concurrency'] == case['concurrency']
        assert len(samples) == iterations * case['concurrency']
        assert len({(s['worker'], s['iteration']) for s in samples}) == len(samples)
        assert not any(s.get('error') for s in samples)
        http = case['protocol'] in ['h1', 'h2', 'h3']
        response = (case['response_bytes'] if http else
                    0 if 'file_transfer' in case['protocol'] else
                    case['request_bytes'] * case.get('peer_count', 1))
        assert all(s['request_bytes'] == case['request_bytes'] and s['response_bytes'] == response for s in samples)
        latency = sorted(s['latency_ms'] for s in samples)
        assert all(math.isfinite(value) and value >= 0 for value in latency)
        lifecycle = (row['completed_at_ms'] - row['started_at_ms']) / 1000
        elapsed = lifecycle if http else row['data_window_elapsed_ms'] / 1000
        if http:
            usage = row['http_connection_usage']
            assert usage['reuse_connections'] == case['reuse_connections']
            expected_connections = case['concurrency'] if case['reuse_connections'] else len(samples)
            connection_finding = (None if usage['connections_opened'] == expected_connections else
                                  dict(workload=name, expected_connections=expected_connections,
                                       connections_opened=usage['connections_opened']))
            if not case['reuse_connections']:
                for sample in samples:
                    timing = sample['http_fresh_connection_timing']
                    assert all(math.isfinite(v) and v >= 0 for v in timing.values())
                    assert timing['operation_total_ms'] + 1e-6 >= timing['connection_setup_ms'] + sample['latency_ms']
        assert elapsed > 0 and lifecycle > 0
        after = row['metrics_after']['metrics']['transport']
        before = row['metrics_before']['metrics']['transport']
        counters = {k: v - before.get(k, 0) for k, v in after.items() if isinstance(v, (int, float))}
        for key in ['protocol_error_events', 'internal_error_events', 'body_timeout_events', 'idle_timeout_events']:
            assert counters.get(key, 0) == 0, (name, key, counters)
        summaries.append(dict(
            workload=name, samples=len(samples), errors=0, data_seconds=elapsed,
            lifecycle_seconds=lifecycle, request_bytes=sum(s['request_bytes'] for s in samples),
            response_bytes=sum(s['response_bytes'] for s in samples),
            requests_per_second=len(samples) / elapsed,
            gbit_per_second=len(samples) * (case['request_bytes'] + response) * 8 / elapsed / 1e9,
            lifecycle_gbit_per_second=len(samples) * (case['request_bytes'] + response) * 8 / lifecycle / 1e9,
            p50_ms=statistics.median(latency), p95_ms=latency[int((len(latency)-1)*.95)],
            p99_ms=latency[int((len(latency)-1)*.99)],
            server_process=row['metrics_after']['metrics']['process'],
            client_process=row.get('client_process_metrics'), transport_counter_deltas=counters,
        ))
        summaries[-1]['throughput_window'] = 'HTTP lifecycle' if http else 'WAMP data window'
        if http:
            summaries[-1]['connection_usage'] = row['http_connection_usage']
            summaries[-1]['validation_findings'] = [] if connection_finding is None else [connection_finding]
            if not case['reuse_connections']:
                total = sorted(s['http_fresh_connection_timing']['operation_total_ms'] for s in samples)
                summaries[-1]['operation_total_p99_ms'] = total[int((len(total)-1)*.99)]
    assert len(summaries) == 2 * len(cases)
    assert len({w['workload'] for w in summaries}) == len(summaries)
    return summaries


def main():
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
    cases = scenario_cases()
    scenario = OUT / 'resource_boundary.toml'
    with scenario.open('x') as stream:
        stream.write('name = "resource_boundary"\ndescription = "Native-only checked resource allocation comparison; unchanged AOT clients/router and cryptography."\n')
        for case in cases:
            for warmup in [True, False]:
                values = dict(case)
                if warmup:
                    values['name'] = 'warmup_' + case['name']
                    values['iterations'] = warmup_iterations(case)
                stream.write('\n[[workloads]]\n')
                for key, value in values.items():
                    stream.write(f'{key} = {json.dumps(value)}\n')
    assert tomllib.loads(scenario.read_text())['workloads']
    identity = {str(p): digest(p) for p in [*EXPECTED, LAUNCHER, scenario, Path(__file__)]}
    assert all(identity[str(p)] == expected for p, expected in EXPECTED.items())
    write_new(OUT / 'inputs.json', dict(
        hashes=identity, cases=cases, baseline_source='d1873a46',
        baseline_library_note='Frozen SA-007 native library, identical production sources to d1873a46.',
        native_diff=subprocess.check_output(['git', 'diff', '--', 'native/transport/ct_ffi/src/runtime/state.rs', 'native/transport/ct_ffi/src/runtime/ffi.rs'], cwd=ROOT, text=True),
        driver_diff=subprocess.check_output(['git', 'diff', '--', 'native/bench/src/bin/http_stream.rs'], cwd=ROOT, text=True),
        driver_note='Both variants use the same corrected HTTP/1 sender-readiness driver. Two earlier old-driver baseline attempts rejected reconnects and are retained separately.',
        allocator_source=(ROOT / 'native/transport/ct_ffi/src/runtime/resource_handles.rs').read_text(),
        candidate_source_hashes={p: digest(ROOT / p) for p in [
            'native/transport/ct_ffi/src/runtime/resource_handles.rs',
            'native/transport/ct_ffi/src/runtime/state.rs',
            'native/transport/ct_ffi/src/runtime/ffi.rs']},
        platform=subprocess.check_output(['uname', '-a'], text=True).strip(),
        toolchain_observed_now={
            'rustc': subprocess.check_output(['rustc', '-Vv'], text=True).strip(),
            'dart': subprocess.check_output(['dart', '--version'], text=True, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT).strip(),
            'note': 'Current local toolchain; frozen AOT service/worker hashes identify retained prior-checkpoint build inputs, not a rebuild during these timings.',
        },
    ))
    runs = []
    for i, variant in enumerate(['baseline', 'patched', 'patched', 'baseline', 'baseline', 'patched'], 1):
        name = f'{i:02}-{variant}'
        preflight(name)
        assert all(digest(Path(p)) == sha for p, sha in identity.items())
        result = OUT / f'{name}.jsonl'
        command = [str(DRIVER), '--dart', str(LAUNCHER), '--bench-main', str(SERVICE),
                   '--wamp-worker-executable', str(WORKER), '--native-lib', str(LIBRARIES[variant]),
                   '--scenario', str(scenario), '--router-worker-counts', '1',
                   '--native-runtime-thread-counts', '4', '--results', str(result),
                   '--artifact-dir', str(OUT / name)]
        entry = dict(variant=variant, command=command, cpu_before=cpu(), started_at=time.time())
        write_new(OUT / f'{name}.started.json', entry)
        print(f'Starting {name}', flush=True)
        try:
            with (OUT / f'{name}.log').open('x') as log:
                run = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=1200)
            entry.update(return_code=run.returncode)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            entry.update(return_code=None, timeout_seconds=1200)
            raise
        finally:
            entry.update(cpu_after=cpu(), finished_at=time.time())
            write_new(OUT / f'{name}.finished.json', entry)
        run.check_returncode()
        entry.update(workloads=summarize(result, cases), raw_sha256=digest(result))
        entry['validation_findings'] = [f for w in entry['workloads'] for f in w.get('validation_findings', [])]
        entry['strict_validation_passed'] = not entry['validation_findings']
        write_new(OUT / f'{name}.summary.json', entry)
        runs.append(entry)
        print(f'Collected {name}: {len(entry["workloads"])} workloads; {len(entry["validation_findings"])} strict findings', flush=True)
        time.sleep(3)
    comparison = {}
    for case in cases:
        name = case['name']
        item = {}
        for variant in LIBRARIES:
            rows = [w for r in runs if r['variant'] == variant for w in r['workloads'] if w['workload'] == name]
            item[variant] = {k: dict(median=statistics.median(w[k] for w in rows),
                                    min=min(w[k] for w in rows), max=max(w[k] for w in rows))
                             for k in ['requests_per_second', 'gbit_per_second', 'lifecycle_gbit_per_second', 'p50_ms', 'p95_ms', 'p99_ms']}
        if case['protocol'] in ['h1', 'h2', 'h3'] and not case['reuse_connections']:
            for variant in LIBRARIES:
                values = [w['operation_total_p99_ms'] for r in runs if r['variant'] == variant
                          for w in r['workloads'] if w['workload'] == name]
                item[variant]['operation_total_p99_ms'] = dict(median=statistics.median(values), min=min(values), max=max(values))
        item['throughput_delta_percent'] = 100 * (item['patched']['gbit_per_second']['median'] / item['baseline']['gbit_per_second']['median'] - 1)
        comparison[name] = item
    findings = [dict(run=i+1, variant=r['variant'], **f) for i, r in enumerate(runs) for f in r['validation_findings']]
    write_new(OUT / 'comparison.json', dict(runs=runs, comparison=comparison,
        strict_validation_passed=not findings, validation_findings=findings,
        caveat='Shared-host observation, not proof of zero overhead. GBit/s is application request plus response bytes, not wire bytes. Files count one-way payload only. Separate warmup workloads do not share sessions with measured workloads. HTTP throughput uses lifecycle elapsed; request latency excludes setup, with setup-inclusive p99 also recorded for fresh connections.'))
    if findings:
        print(f'Strict comparison failed: {len(findings)} unexpected connection counts; all processes retained.', flush=True)
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
